title: The anti-Dunning-Kruger category: self-calibration as the corpus's measured stance
status: recorded - instrument built, demo-validated; human subject runs pending
concept: Dunning-Kruger (1999): the least competent are the most overconfident; confidence falls as competence rises. The corpus's own recorded output is the INVERSE curve by construction: every probe published its null first and confidence decreased with depth (19/45 at chance, 2 vs 1.78 expected, 4.6%, 1.6%, 70/366). This category makes that stance measurable in a person.

instrument.method: 20 general-knowledge items, subject answers + states confidence 50-100; scored as overconfidence index (mean confidence - mean accuracy, points), Brier score (0 = perfect, 0.25 = random), and calibration curve (realized accuracy per confidence bin)
instrument.instrument_null: THE FLOOR IS +25 PTS, NOT 0: random confidence is uniform 50-100 (mean 75) vs random accuracy 50%, so a random subject over-states by ~25 points. The 50-100 scale has no 0-anchor. A subject must exceed +25 to show true overconfidence beyond the scale's own bias.

demo_validation.reading: the instrument separates overconfident from calibrated subjects; sample DK subject: confidence 83% vs accuracy 50% = +33 pts, Brier 0.331 (worse than random)

human_culture_connections.school: the 'DK valley' in learning: novices overrate exam readiness; the worst scorers show the largest overconfidence gap (Kruger & Dunning 1999; the effect shrinks with teaching)
human_culture_connections.jobs: impostor syndrome in high performers is the mirror side (underconfidence among the competent); novice overconfidence is documented in medicine, driving, and finance
human_culture_connections.driving: classic finding: ~90% of drivers rate themselves above average (Svenson 1981) - arithmetic impossibility, the purest cultural DK instance
human_culture_connections.finance: overconfident traders trade more and earn less (Barber & Odean 2000) - the market price of the +25 floor
human_culture_connections.activities: chess, poker, prediction markets: calibration improves with domain expertise and explicit feedback - the corpus's own pattern
human_culture_connections.corpus_parallel: the epoch probe series behaved like a calibrated expert: null-first, confidence fell with depth, final verdict 'coincidence-scale'

test_usage.interpret: overconfidence_index > 25 pts = true overconfidence beyond instrument floor; Brier > 0.25 = worse than guessing; calibration curve should be monotone (higher stated confidence -> higher realized accuracy)

honest_limits: the corpus's 'anti-DK record' is a meta-reading of its own published nulls, not a psychological measurement of anyone
the instrument is validated only on simulated subjects; no human data recorded yet
overconfidence is a property of subjects, not of numbers - this category stands apart from the arithmetic probes and should not be read as evidence about the epoch
the +25 floor means the scale itself is biased; a 0-100 anchored scale would set the null near 0 and is the recommended v2
